title: Measuring Surface Syntax Variants
description: Count characters, lines, punctuation characters, and tokens across syntax variants of the same max(a, b) function.

steps.description: Store the Python-style and C-style versions of max(a, b) in VARIANTS, with space at lines 20-21 for your team's third variant.
Define PUNCT and write measure(src) to return a 4-tuple of character count, line count, punctuation count, and space-split token count.

steps.question: How many punctuation characters in PUNCT appear in the Python-style variant vs. the C-style variant?
steps.answer: Python-style has 6 punctuation characters (two parentheses, one comma, and three colons), while C-style has 13 (four parentheses, one comma, six braces, and two semicolons).

steps.description: Loop over VARIANTS.items() to print the aligned comparison table and review the team discussion prompts.
Inspect the computed counts (c, l, p, w) for the Python-style variant as its table row is printed.
